raw_response:
I’m planting cotton again on all 7 mu. I’ve done this many years, and on this land I know roughly how it behaves. Wheat and maize turn faster, but for my small household and with some people working outside, cotton fits better because I can spread the work out, even if picking time is still tiring. The extension fellow has said not to push fertilizer too hard, but if I go too low and the cotton stays weak, then the whole year suffers. So this year I’ll use a moderate amount, about the same as last year, maybe a little cleaner in timing. I’ll put most fertilizer before or at planting, then add a smaller topdress when squares and bolls are coming. Water costs money from the well, so I won’t irrigate blindly. I’ll give water after planting if the soil is dry, then again around flowering and boll setting if rain is short. For pests, cotton cannot be ignored. If aphids or bollworms show up, I’ll spray; if pressure is light, I won’t waste money. I still do things mostly the practical way: what worked on my own field, and what nearby farmers are doing this year.
